gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the stylus costs per playing hour. Fluance's own store prices both the RT81's ATN95E and the RT81+'s AT-VMN95E at $52.99, each rated 300–500 hours, so both decks cost about $0.11–$0.18 per hour in stylus wear. The AT-LP70X's VM95C cartridge takes the same VM95-series styli as the RT81+, while the RT81's AT95E does not.
standout_why: I compared against valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives, which gives wow and flutter, S/N and phono gain but no stylus life, stylus price or cost per hour. I also checked platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp, which gives prices, wow and flutter and platter weight but says nothing about stylus life or replacement cost. The fewbetter.com result loaded with unrelated products (mini PC, kettle and others) and no turntable data. I did not open the other ten results.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. Between the two Fluance decks, the RT81+ does not cost less to keep running: both replacement styli are $52.99 and both are rated 300–500 h. What the RT81+ adds is a VM95-series cartridge that takes better styli later, up to the $159.99 AT-VMN95ML microlinear on Fluance's own store. The RT81's AT95E cannot take those. The AT-LP70X uses the same VM95 family (VM95C), so a beginner can fit an elliptical later with the same $52.99 VMN95E. That makes the LP70X's upgrade path the same as the RT81+'s, which supports ChatGPT's beginner pick.
